title: Slow-Roasted Dibi-Style Leg of Lamb
author: ‘Shepherd’ (Shepherd Song Farm site persona), recipe used with permission from Pierre Thiam
desc: A leg of lamb rubbed with thyme, Dijon, cumin, salt, pepper and oil, sealed with sliced onions and a quarter cup of water in kraft paper and roasted 8 hours at 275 °F until the meat pulls away from the bone and is tender.
longDesc: A slow-roasted take on dibi, the grilled lamb sold in Dakar’s dibiteries, published on Shepherd Song Farm on 25 August 2018 (page metadata last modified 3 March 2025) and credited ‘Used with permission from Chef Pierre Thiam’. The oven is preheated to 275 °F; thyme, Dijon mustard, cumin, salt, pepper and oil are mixed and rubbed over the lamb; a baking sheet is lined with kraft paper (or parchment, or a paper grocery bag in a pinch) large enough to enclose the lamb; sliced onions are spread in the centre, the lamb set on top and the water poured around the leg; the paper is folded tightly around lamb and onions to make a fully sealed package and roasted 8 hours. The meat is cut into bite-sized pieces and served with the caramelised onions, or arranged on a platter with baguette chunks, extra mustard and the Tamarind Kani Mustard Sauce (SEN094). THE LEG’S WEIGHT IS NOT PRINTED — a material absence for an 8-hour roast for 8 — and is not inferred.
ingredients: 1 leg of lamb — weight not printed
2 tablespoons Dijon mustard, plus more for serving
Baguettes, for serving — quantity not printed
Tamarind kani sauce (SEN094), for serving — quantity not printed
1 sheet of kraft paper, parchment or a paper grocery bag
equipment: Kraft paper (or parchment, or a paper grocery bag)
steps: Mix the thyme, mustard, cumin, salt, pepper and oil and rub over the leg of lamb.
Line a baking sheet with kraft paper large enough to enclose the lamb. Spread the sliced onions in the centre, set the lamb on top and carefully pour the water around the leg.
Fold the paper tightly around the lamb and onions to make a fully sealed package. A clean paper grocery bag tied shut also works.
Cut the meat into bite-sized pieces and serve with the caramelised onions, or arrange on a platter with baguette chunks, extra mustard and kani sauce.
chefTips: The one doneness cue is that the meat pulls away from the bone and is tender.
Seal the paper fully so the steam stays in.
275 °F is the only numeric oven temperature printed for any recipe in this collection.
commonMistakes: Leaving gaps in the paper package.
Guessing the leg size without checking the weight — the page gives none.
Cutting before the meat falls from the bone.
healthBenefits: Slow cooking with onions makes the meat very tender; the cumin and mustard are the only seasonings.
culturalNote: Small eateries called dibiteries ‘serve slow roasted dibi lamb and goat meat as a street food’ in Senegal and elsewhere in Africa — the only dibiterie documentation this research could source. This oven version is not the charcoal-grilled street dish (SEN073, SEN074).
sources: Title as printed: ‘Slow Roasted Dibi Lamb Recipe’; recipe name ‘Dibi-Style Leg of Lamb’. Byline as printed: ‘Shepherd’ — a site persona, not a personal name; flagged. Source attribution as printed: ‘Used with permission from Chef Pierre Thiam’, whose book ‘Senegal: Modern Senegalese Recipes from the Source to the Bowl’ and website are named. Published 25 August 2018 (metadata last modified 3 March 2025). Yield 8 servings; prep 15 minutes, cook 8 hours, total 8 hours 15 minutes. SINGLE-PASS.

Cue (verbatim): ‘the meat pulls away from the bone and is tender’. The only numeric oven temperature in this collection: 275 °F. Equipment: 1 sheet of kraft paper, parchment or a paper grocery bag in a pinch.
ABSENT, not estimated: the weight of the leg of lamb; the quantity of baguettes; the quantity of kani sauce for serving.
